title: Real players on the dogfood: ExoPlayer and AVPlayer play jellyscale's own streams
description: Every streaming decision so far was checked on hls.js in Chromium only. No ExoPlayer client or AVPlayer client (Swiftfin) has played a jellyscale stream (Findroid and Android TV's direct play send no token on media requests and are not targets, D-026), which the Phase 0 report left open (spikes/README.md, remaining risks 1 and 2), and the decision engine answers direct play to any client whose profile has no fMP4 HLS entry (internal/playback/decide.go). Before more is built on the segment format (JS-054), the owner plays films on real devices against the dogfood, and the lead records what each client asked for and what it played. Web-first stays the plan; this is a check that the format holds.
acceptanceCriteria: The owner plays, against the dogfood, on Jellyfin for Android with its built-in ExoPlayer player (not the web player in its WebView, and with the external player option off) and on Swiftfin with its native AVPlayer player, both read from source as sending their token on every media request (D-030): a direct play, an HEVC or 4K film that transcodes, a seek, an audio switch, a text and an image subtitle. The record names the engine that played each, from the app's setting and the server's log; a run on any other player the app offers proves nothing about the family and is recorded as such (a family left without a run on its engine falls under the next criterion)

An app whose player sends no token is recorded as refused (D-005) and not supported (D-026), never as a failure to chase, and no task comes of it; a player family with no client that sends a token is listed in docs/status.md as not proven (no client that sends a token), not a pass

Each client's PlaybackInfo request and the server's decision are recorded from the dogfood's logs, taken from JS-153's decision line (no titles or paths in the record), with what the viewer saw; for each client, whether its request carries an AudioStreamIndex the viewer did not pick (taken from the item's named track) and which track played when the viewer's saved language is not the file's default (D-034)
Each failure becomes a task in tasks/prd.json, placed before JS-054 when it concerns the segment format
docs/status.md says which clients have played which paths
An HEVC HDR copy and its fallback are played once in a browser with an HEVC decoder (E2E_HEVC=1) and recorded; until then docs/status.md says 'checked with ffmpeg only'
Streamyfin's player entries in compat/clients.yaml are corrected from what the device sends

On each client played: a server address typed with a trailing slash still signs in; whether it asks for the subtitle playlist, and what its viewer sees, is recorded; what its viewer reads when a sign-in is refused by JS-145 (403 with Retry-After, D-020) is recorded in docs/access.md, and no task comes of an app's wording

Whether each device's profile declares Dolby Vision is recorded. On one that does: a profile 5 film and a profile 8.1 film from the dogfood are played, with what PlaybackInfo decided (direct play, copy or re-encode) and what the viewer saw. A profile 5 film re-encoded for a client that declares it becomes a task. If neither device declares it, or the dogfood holds no profile 5 film, docs/status.md says profile 5 on a client that declares Dolby Vision is not proven (D-021)

Each played app's direct-play, HLS, subtitle and download requests seen on the dogfood are compared with what was read from source (D-030): a media request that arrives with no token from an app listed as sending one moves that app to not supported in docs/status.md (D-026), and no task comes of it

For each app played: whether it asked for a Trickplay route, and whether its sign-in screen offered a code (Quick Connect), with what the server answered and what the viewer saw (nothing, a missing preview, an error); an error a viewer sees is brought to the product owner (BL-222), and no route is built in this task

Moonfin on an Android TV device signs in and plays one direct play and one film that transcodes, recorded like the others with the engine that played; if it is not run, docs/status.md says no Android TV app has played; on a film with several subtitle tracks, the subtitle index Moonfin asked for and the track it resolved to are recorded, with its subtitle mode (finding 5, D-038)
notes: Needs the owner's devices and about an hour; the lead prepares the test list and reads the logs. Widened by the product owner's direction review (2026-11-19): goals 1 and 3 are claimed for every client and proven for one. Findroid and Android TV are not targets (owner, 2026-11-20, D-026); The ExoPlayer client is Jellyfin for Android's built-in player and the AVPlayer client is Swiftfin's native player, both read from source as sending their token (product owner, 2026-11-20, D-030); a device still has to show it. No Fluster run is part of this task (owner, 2026-11-20, D-027). D-073: moved up; needs the owner's hour and no build slot. First slice: criteria 1 to 5 and 10. Criteria 6 to 9, 11 and 12 are recorded where the same hour shows them, and otherwise left open in docs/status.md, not chased. Dropped (D-126 and the pivot, D-107): Jellyfin apps on real players (rules 3 and 4). Octave's players are JS-190 and JS-199.
